name: Irnan

attributes.attribute: an Irish heroine, a daughter of the goddess Conaran who was killed by Goll mac Morna

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Irnan is an Irish heroine. Her mother was the goddess Conaran of the Tuatha Dé Danann. Conaran had three daughters. All three were skilled in magic. The daughters were sent to capture members of the Fianna. They spun a magical web that held the men fast. The hero Goll mac Morna appeared to do battle. He killed two of Irnan's sisters. The web held until he threatened Irnan with death. She agreed to break the spell. Instead she turned into a monster. She demanded that the three Fianna warriors fight her in single combat. The heroes Oisín, Oscar, and Celta refused. They feared her power. Their leader Fionn mac Cumhaill came to fight. Goll stepped in and killed Irnan. The story is not tied to any major myth cycle. It reflects a common theme of heroes killing hag monsters. Some believe it hides an ancient creation tale. In that tale a goddess is killed to make the earth.
